judgment.observations: The reconstruction captures the electronics workbench and major objects, but simplifies the reference substantially. Its framing is more frontal and orderly, with more blank wall and a less densely cluttered desktop. The monitor is smaller and lower in the composition; the oscilloscope has a much simpler control panel, and the central multimeter appears smaller. The keyboard, meters, hanging pliers, drawer cabinets and overhead lamp occupy broadly similar regions. Numerous small tools, cables, containers and equipment details are missing or reduced, producing fewer overlaps. The reference’s tangled leads and layered papers become a sparse, cleaner arrangement. The lamp lacks the reference’s prominent rounded housing and complex arm connections. Surfaces are pale, matte and softly shaded compared with the reference’s darker plastics, reflective metal, saturated accents and worn desktop. Render grain also obscures fine detail.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The reconstructed bench appears shallower and the viewpoint more level, although projection and framing could explain some of this difference. Cable crossings and tool placement suggest flatter layering than in the reference. Some equipment bases and the right-side lamp/support assembly have less convincing visible contact cues, but their actual depth, support and hidden connections cannot be established from these images.
